about: Competition and venue tidy-up for the Belgravian (Steve, 14 Nov 2026). build.py reads this file. Each entry renames the tags in 'forms' (matched loosely: capitals, punctuation, 'Championship(s)', a final plural) to 'into'; 'from'/'to' limit the years. Only entries with apply: true act; medium and low ones wait for Steve's yes/no. Steve's earlier rules in build.py (Southern, Surrey League, Inter-Counties, London to Brighton, British Athletics League) still come first. Age-group versions stay apart; a town stays apart from the venues in it.

forms: Norwich Union European Trials & AAA Championships
evidence: Steve, 14 Nov 2026: the AAA Championships became the British Championships

Wikipedia, AAA Championships: the AAA Championships (to 2006) 'served as the de facto British Championships'; Wikipedia, British Athletics Championships: 'established in 2007, replacing the AAA Championships' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAA_Championships, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Athletics_Championships)
The archive prints 'Norwich Union European Trials & AAA Championships' (2006) and 'British Championships' (2006) for the same meeting
The separate UK Championships (1977-93, 1997) ran alongside the AAA and are kept apart

One Games under its successive names: British Empire Games (1930-50), British Empire and Commonwealth Games (1954-66), British Commonwealth Games (1970-74), Commonwealth Games (1978 on) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games)

The archive uses each name in its own years (Empire Games 1929-1950s, British Empire and Commonwealth 1962-66, British Commonwealth 1969-74, Commonwealth 1970 on); later mentions of the older names are look-backs
The International Cross Country Championships (1903-72) became the IAAF World Cross Country Championships from 1973 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships)
Recommend YES if you see them as one race, as with the AAA; NO keeps the old International (home countries) and the World event apart
The 'National' is the English Cross Country Championships (English Cross Country Association/Union); the archive uses both names 1935-2007, same senior/junior/youth races and venues
442 items say National, 21 say English; no item uses both for different races

forms: South of England 12 Stage Road Relay
evidence: Southern became SEAA (South of England AA); you already merged the Southern/SEAA cross-country and track championships (8 Nov 2026) on the same basis
Southern 12 Stage 1979-2003, SEAA 12-Stage 1998-2008: the same road relay
Southern became SEAA; same 6-stage road relay under both names

The National Road Relay (12 stages, Sutton Park from the 1970s) is run by the AAA/England Athletics; 'AAA 12-Stage Road Relay' 2000-05 and 'National Road Relay' are held at Sutton Coldfield/Sutton Park
'National Road Relay Championship' (1966-70, Leicester) is left out: before 1967 'national road relay' can mean the London to Brighton relay
The AAA (later England Athletics) National 6-stage road relay under its two names
One league, printed with and without 'Athletics' (2003-08)
The same league with the words in either order (1977-2008); 'Ladies' used once in 1991

The national Young Athletes' League under its sponsors' names: Dunlop (1983-85), Girobank (1989), Woolworth's (1991-92), McDonald's (1995-99), then 'National YA League' (to 2006): the same track and field matches (Deangate, Crawley, Guildford, Battersea)
The Lily B League (girls) and the Surrey Young Athletes cross-country league are left apart
The national club cup under its sponsors' names: GRE (Guardian Royal Exchange) Cup / Gold Cup 1981-95, Guardian (Insurance) Gold Cup 1995-97, then Gold Cup: same track and field club cup
The Jubilee Cup (the lower-tier cup) is left apart
1998-2001 Gold Cup rounds printed as 'British Athletics League Gold Cup'; probably the same cup, run with the league
The lower-tier national club cup under its sponsors' names (GRE, Guardian)
1992-2007: the European Champion Clubs Cup; 'Championship' and 'Cup' look like the same competition in the same years (1993-97)

'Southern Amateur Athletic League' is used for current matches up to 1968 (later only in look-backs, B175-14, B181-11); 'Southern League' starts in 1969 (B172-13), same track and field club matches and venues (Battersea Park, Croydon, White City)
I could not confirm that the 1969 league was the old league renamed rather than a new one: please say yes or no
